assessment.title: What's Your Retirement Paycheck Score?
assessment.subtitle: Answer a few quick questions to see how ready your savings are to become a dependable monthly paycheck, and which areas to focus on first.
bullets: A score for each of the 5 steps of the Retirement Paycheck Blueprint
Your top 2 focus areas, and what to do about them

questions.text: Do you know how much monthly income you'll need in retirement?

options.label: Yes, I have a written monthly budget for retirement

questions.text: Do you know how much of that income will come from Social Security, pensions, or other dependable sources?
Do you have a plan for which accounts you'll draw from first, and how much each year?
Do you know roughly how much of your savings is in pre-tax accounts (like a traditional IRA or 401(k)) versus Roth or taxable accounts?
Have you looked at how taxes, including required minimum distributions, could affect your retirement income?
Has anyone reviewed your situation for opportunities like Roth conversions or tax-smart withdrawal order?
If the market dropped 25% in your first year of retirement, do you know how it would affect your income?

options.label: Yes, I have a plan for that

questions.text: Do you have a plan to pay for long-term care if you or your spouse ever need it?
questions.help: Home care, assisted living, or nursing care.

questions.text: If you passed away first, does your spouse or partner know what income they'd have?
Do you have an up-to-date will or trust (reviewed in the last 5 years)?
Are the beneficiaries on your retirement accounts and insurance policies current?
Have you named someone to make financial and medical decisions if you can't (power of attorney, health care directive)?
How often do you review your whole retirement plan, not just your investments?
Do all your financial documents and accounts live in one organized place your family could find?

qualifiers.text: When do you plan to retire (or did you)?
Roughly how much have you saved for retirement (not counting your home)?
qualifiers.help: A range is fine. This helps us point you to the right next step.

bands.label: Getting Started
bands.headline: You've got some important gaps, and that's exactly why you're here.
bands.message: Most people we meet start here. The good news: a few decisions made now can make a big difference in how confident you feel about retirement.

bands.label: Building Momentum
bands.headline: You've done some things right, but there are gaps that could cost you.
bands.message: You have a foundation. Your focus areas below show where a plan could make the biggest difference.

bands.label: On Solid Ground
bands.headline: You're ahead of most people. A few refinements could matter a lot.
bands.message: Your plan is in good shape. Fine-tuning your focus areas could help your income last and keep more of it in your pocket.

bands.label: Retirement Ready
bands.headline: Excellent. You've covered the big pieces.
bands.message: An annual review keeps a strong plan strong as laws, markets, and your life change.

income.low: You don't yet have a clear picture of your retirement paycheck: what you need, what's coming in, and the gap between them. This is the foundation everything else builds on.
income.mid: You have a rough picture. Turning it into a written monthly income plan shows exactly where your paycheck comes from each year.
income.high: Strong. You know your numbers and your income sources.

tax.low: Taxes could take a bigger bite of your retirement income than you expect. A tax plan looks at when and how to draw from each account.
tax.mid: You've thought about taxes. A year-by-year tax timeline can reveal opportunities you may be missing.
tax.high: Strong. You're managing retirement taxes deliberately.

protect.low: A market drop, a long-term care need, or the loss of a spouse could disrupt your income. These risks can be planned for.
protect.mid: Some protections are in place. Check the gaps, especially long-term care and survivor income.
protect.high: Strong. You've planned for the major risks.

legacy.low: Without current documents and beneficiaries, your family could face delays, costs, and hard decisions. This is often the quickest area to improve.
legacy.mid: You've started. Updating documents and beneficiaries keeps your wishes in force.
legacy.high: Strong. Your legacy documents look current.

review.low: Plans drift as laws, markets, and life change. A yearly review keeps everything working together.
review.mid: Reviewing more regularly, and getting organized, helps your family as much as it helps you.
review.high: Strong. You keep your plan current and organized.
